what: Free-Living Wearable Accelerometry for the Physio Ecosystem
title: Free-Living Wearable Accelerometry for the Physio Ecosystem
text: PhysioWearable analyzes free-living tri-axial accelerometry. covers CSV ingestion, gravity-based calibration, ENMO, non-wear detection, step detection, physical-activity intensity classification, bout summaries, optional conversion common PhysioExperiment model.

title: Free-Living Wearable Accelerometry for the Physio Ecosystem
Free-Living Wearable Accelerometry for the Physio Ecosystem
code: library(PhysioWearable)  sampling_rate <- 50 time <- seq(0, 20, by = 1 / sampling_rate) acceleration <- cbind(   x = 0,   y = 0,   z = 1 + 0.4 * sin(2 * pi * 1.8 * time) )  enmo <- computeENMO(   acceleration,   sampling_rate = sampling_rate,   epoch_sec = 5,   unit = "mg" ) steps <- detectSteps(acceleration, sampling_rate)  enmo steps$n_steps

what: PhysioWearable: Free-Living Wearable Accelerometry for the Physio Ecosystem — PhysioWearable-package
title: PhysioWearable: Free-Living Wearable Accelerometry for the Physio Ecosystem — PhysioWearable-package
text: Free-living physical-activity analysis raw tri-axial accelerometer data, following GGIR methodology. Computes Euclidean-Norm-Minus-One (ENMO) acceleration metric epoch aggregation, gravity-based auto-calibration (van Hees et al. 2014), non-wear detection, step detection, physical-activity intensity classification bout detection, ingests raw accelerometer exports (GENEActiv / ActiGraph / Axivity CSV) PhysioExperiment objects.

title: Gravity-based accelerometer auto-calibration — autoCalibrateAccel
text: Estimates per-axis gain offset force acceleration magnitude 1 g still periods, following GGIR sphere-fitting method (van Hees et al. 2014). Still (non-movement) windows identified low per-axis standard deviation; mean orientations lie unit sphere ideally-calibrated device, gain/offset fitted iteratively projecting onto sphere. Correction (accel - offset) * scale.
